statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete: 58/58 checks judged across five representative paths.

page.notes: Public multilingual card-game catalog and app-like game templates. Covered homepage, single-player, multiplayer, personalization, and 404; did not cover all games because they reuse shared templates, nor multiplayer matchmaking completion or the hidden report submission.

paths.description: Homepage and game catalog, representing discovery, navigation, consent, and public content.
Solitaire, representing the primary single-player game template and repeated menu interaction.
Hearts, representing multiplayer/table-game templates and player state.
Player avatar customization, representing settings and saved personalization.
Invalid game route, representing HTTP/navigation recovery.

findings.summary: The site does not follow the system dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is visually unchanged from the normal capture; the computed root color-scheme is normal and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide system-driven dark surface/text tokens, retaining the existing manual preference as an override.

findings.summary: Motion preferences are not wired to the game’s effects.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the stylesheet probe found no reduced-motion rule, while the page loads fireworks effects and exposes confetti/holiday-effect settings.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce layer that disables fireworks, confetti, decorative transitions, and auto motion.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences do not change the interface, and controls retain contrast failures.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast screenshot remains visually unchanged; Lighthouse reports contrast failures including 2.19:1 themed links and 4.42:1 consent action text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use forced-colors/prefers-contrast styles and system colors for controls, text, and focus indicators.

findings.summary: Game and route state changes are abrupt.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition usage, while primary actions and full-page game links replace state without directional continuity.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-document game state and cross-document game navigation with View Transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: A first-visit consent wall obscures the entire catalog and every game.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360 px screenshots show an opaque modal over the primary content before interaction; on mobile it consumes nearly the full viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize the initial consent surface, keep equal accept/reject controls, and avoid blocking access to the game where legally possible.

findings.summary: Overlays are custom ARIA divs rather than native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found zero dialog, popover, or details elements but two role=dialog custom divs, including the blocking consent UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows and popover/details for transient disclosure, preserving focus management and light-dismiss semantics.

findings.summary: The primary play journey is interrupted before users can interact.
findings.evidence: Every representative game screenshot shows the consent wall covering the board and controls on first visit, adding a required detour before play.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow immediate non-tracking play or reduce consent to a compact, clearly reversible choice that does not cover the board.

findings.summary: Some controls are inaccessible or too small for non-pointer users.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies the 40x32 mobile-menu button with no accessible name and multiple social links only 17 px high; keyboard focus itself is visible when present.
findings.suggestedFix: Name the menu button and enlarge/space interactive targets to at least the guidance minimum while retaining focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: Non-critical consent and analytics dependencies dominate the initial network.
findings.evidence: HAR: 89 requests and 1,854,791 transferred bytes; 19 third-party requests transfer 701,861 bytes, including 403 KB from the CMP and 299 KB from Google tags.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate and defer non-essential third-party code, consolidate analytics, and load consent vendor detail only when opened.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript adds substantial startup cost without core game value.
findings.evidence: The two Google tag scripts alone transfer about 299 KB, the CMP SDK about 127 KB, and Lighthouse interactive time is 9.2-10.0 s despite good paint metrics.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit tag/CMP coverage, remove duplicate or unused tags, and conditionally load vendor code after a relevant choice.

findings.summary: The mobile menu has no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse button-name fails on button#mobile-menu on both homepage and Solitaire; it has no text, aria-label, aria-labelledby, or title.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an accurate accessible name and expose expanded/controlled state with aria-expanded and aria-controls.

findings.summary: Game-theme and consent text do not meet minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports themed links at 2.19:1, board text at 3.77:1, and the accept button at 4.42:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens and verify normal, themed, and consent states at WCAG AA contrast.

findings.summary: In-page game action links point to missing focus targets.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports New Game, Restart, Pause, and Options hash links as skip links without valid targets; the document also contains two H1 elements in game state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real controls for actions, valid target IDs for navigable sections, and a single coherent page heading hierarchy.

findings.summary: The game template logs a browser inspector cookie issue.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices is 0.77 on Solitaire and reports an Issues-panel third-party-cookie problem from a.pub.network.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the third-party-cookie dependency or migrate it to a privacy-preserving storage posture.

findings.summary: The site does not publish a working sitemap.
findings.evidence: A request to /sitemap.xml returns the site’s Page Not Found HTML; robots.txt is empty. Canonical and hreflang signals otherwise exist.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid XML sitemap for canonical game and locale URLs and reference it from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Game pages lack structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: Open Graph metadata exists, but DOM inspection found no JSON-LD on the homepage despite the site representing a collection of playable games.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org WebSite and VideoGame/Game structured data that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie flags are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff and X-Frame-Options are present, but CSP is absent; both observed first-party cookies lack Secure and country uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a nonce/hash-based CSP and mark HTTPS cookies Secure with the least-permissive appropriate SameSite value.

findings.summary: The initial privacy footprint is disproportionate to a simple card-game visit.
findings.evidence: The banner names 1,017 partners; the load contacts four third-party origins and known Google trackers, transferring 701,861 third-party bytes. No sensitive secret was exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce partner/vendor scope, default to data minimisation globally, and delay analytics/advertising calls until a valid contextual choice.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced policy coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no Content-Security-Policy or Permissions-Policy; HSTS, framing, referrer and nosniff protections are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP (including frame-ancestors) and a restrictive Permissions-Policy matched to features actually used.

findings.summary: The app-like game site is installable in metadata only and has no offline fallback.
findings.evidence: A valid standalone manifest exists, but navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returned no registrations on Solitaire.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker that precaches the game shell and provides an intentional offline page/state for previously visited games.

findings.summary: The localized site is not demonstrably writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: The page publishes six hreflang locales and correct lang=en, but stylesheet inspection found no logical-property signal in the inspected rules and no dir declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical inset/margin/padding properties and set dir from locale so translated layouts remain robust for RTL expansion.

findings.summary: The user-report form omits autocomplete hints.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found labelled name, email, description, device, and location fields, but every field has an empty autocomplete attribute value.
findings.suggestedFix: Add appropriate autocomplete tokens such as name, email, and country-name/address-level values, using off only where justified.

findings.summary: Third-party and decorative media cost is high relative to the core interaction.
findings.evidence: HAR transfers 1.85 MB on the homepage: 702 KB third party and 1.05 MB images, including a 156 KB decorative stadium image and multiple tag/CMP bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer vendors, simplify the event theme, optimize decorative images, and enforce a page-weight budget for non-game assets.

findings.summary: Repeated menu exercise shows substantial retained-heap growth that needs investigation.
findings.evidence: Heap summaries rise from 17,365,169 bytes/364,950 nodes to 24,988,197 bytes/530,849 nodes after ten menu open/close cycles. The separate-session comparison makes confidence medium and does not isolate a constructor leak.
findings.suggestedFix: Reproduce in one long-lived session with baseline/target/final snapshots, force GC between snapshots, then remove accumulating listeners, nodes, or late-loaded vendor state.

taskList.title: Make non-tracking play immediately accessible and replace the full-screen first-visit consent wall with a compact, reversible choice.
Fix accessible names, contrast, hash-action semantics, and touch target sizing across shared templates.
Reduce the consent/analytics partner footprint and defer third-party scripts until a valid contextual choice.
Deploy nonce/hash CSP, Permissions-Policy, and secure least-permissive cookie attributes.
Add system-driven dark, reduced-motion, and high-contrast modes.
Use native dialog/popover primitives for modal and transient overlays.
Add a service worker with an intentional offline shell/fallback.
Investigate repeated-interaction heap growth with same-session GC-controlled snapshots.
Publish a valid sitemap and accurate game/WebSite structured data.
Make localized CSS direction-safe with logical properties and locale-driven dir.
Add form autocomplete tokens and clear browser inspector cookie issues.
Progressively enhance route and state changes with View Transitions.
